title: A new acid-base disturbance
prompt: A 28-year-old woman taking topiramate for epilepsy reports fatigue. Sodium is 140 mEq/L, chloride 113 mEq/L, and bicarbonate 17 mEq/L. Creatinine, lactate, and glucose are normal; urine ketones are negative. She has no diarrhea. Which mechanism best explains these findings?
options: Accumulation of ketoacids from insulin deficiency
Renal bicarbonate loss from carbonic anhydrase inhibition
Accumulation of lactate from tissue hypoperfusion
answer: Renal bicarbonate loss from carbonic anhydrase inhibition
explanation: The anion gap is 10. Topiramate can cause renal bicarbonate loss and hyperchloremic acidosis.

distractorExplanations.Renal bicarbonate loss from carbonic anh: The anion gap is 10. Topiramate can cause renal bicarbonate loss and hyperchloremic acidosis.
distractorExplanations.Accumulation of lactate from tissue hypo: Lactate is normal, and the anion gap is not increased.
distractorExplanations.Accumulation of ketoacids from insulin d: Normal glucose and absent ketonuria argue against diabetic ketoacidosis.
distractorExplanations.Gastric hydrogen ion loss: Loss of gastric acid usually produces metabolic alkalosis.
distractorExplanations.Primary alveolar hypoventilation: This produces respiratory acidosis rather than a primary bicarbonate deficit.

title: Painful blurred vision after treatment begins
prompt: A 31-year-old man develops bilateral blurred vision and eye pain 12 days after starting topiramate. Examination shows an acute myopic shift, shallow anterior chambers, and elevated intraocular pressures. Which diagnosis best unifies the ocular findings and medication history?
explanation: Topiramate can cause an acute myopic shift with secondary angle closure, requiring urgent assessment.

distractorExplanations.Drug-associated secondary angle-closure: Topiramate can cause an acute myopic shift with secondary angle closure, requiring urgent assessment.
distractorExplanations.Optic neuritis: Optic nerve inflammation does not explain shallow chambers and high intraocular pressure.
distractorExplanations.Retinal detachment: A retinal lesion does not explain bilateral anterior chamber shallowing.
distractorExplanations.Primary open-angle glaucoma: This is usually gradual and does not cause this acute myopic syndrome.
distractorExplanations.Migraine visual aura: Aura does not account for persistent objective pressure elevation.

title: A stone-forming urinary environment
prompt: A 42-year-old woman taking topiramate presents with colicky flank pain and hematuria. CT identifies a ureteral calculus. She has no infection or hypercalcemia. Which pair of urinary changes associated with her medication favors calcium phosphate stone formation?
options: Higher urine volume and lower urinary calcium
Higher urine pH and lower urinary citrate
Lower urine pH and higher urinary citrate
Lower urine pH and lower urinary uric acid
Higher urine pH and higher urinary citrate
answer: Higher urine pH and lower urinary citrate
explanation: Alkaline urine and reduced citrate favor stone formation during topiramate treatment.

distractorExplanations.Higher urine pH and lower urinary citrat: Alkaline urine and reduced citrate favor stone formation during topiramate treatment.
distractorExplanations.Lower urine pH and higher urinary citrat: Acidic urine favors uric acid precipitation; citrate inhibits calcium crystal formation.
distractorExplanations.Lower urine pH and lower urinary uric ac: Reduced uric acid excretion does not explain this calcium phosphate pattern.
distractorExplanations.Higher urine pH and higher urinary citra: The increased citrate would oppose calcium crystal formation.
distractorExplanations.Higher urine volume and lower urinary ca: Dilution and reduced calcium excretion generally reduce calcium stone risk.

title: A change in classroom performance
prompt: A 20-year-old college student has fewer seizures after topiramate titration but struggles to retrieve familiar words and completes assignments more slowly. Neurologic examination is otherwise unchanged. There are no discrete episodes of impaired awareness. Which explanation is most likely?
explanation: Topiramate can impair word retrieval and processing speed.

distractorExplanations.Medication-associated cognitive slowing: Topiramate can impair word retrieval and processing speed.
distractorExplanations.Recurrent focal impaired-awareness seizu: Continuous difficulty without discrete spells is less consistent with this explanation.
distractorExplanations.Acute dominant-hemisphere infarction: An abrupt focal deficit would be expected rather than difficulty emerging during titration.
distractorExplanations.Primary progressive aphasia: The age and close medication relationship make a neurodegenerative aphasia unlikely.
distractorExplanations.Myasthenia gravis: This causes fatigable weakness, not impaired word retrieval.

title: Heat intolerance during summer activity
prompt: An 8-year-old boy taking topiramate becomes flushed and unusually hot during outdoor activity. His skin is dry despite the heat, and his parent reports much less sweating since therapy began. Which drug-associated effect best explains the presentation?
explanation: Reduced sweating can cause overheating, particularly in children taking topiramate.

distractorExplanations.Oligohidrosis with impaired heat dissipa: Reduced sweating can cause overheating, particularly in children taking topiramate.
distractorExplanations.Serotonin toxicity: Clonus, hyperreflexia, and a serotonergic exposure would support this alternative.
distractorExplanations.Malignant hyperthermia: This usually follows a triggering anesthetic exposure, absent here.
distractorExplanations.Thyroid storm: The history lacks thyroid disease or a broader thyrotoxic syndrome.
distractorExplanations.Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: A dopamine-blocking exposure and marked rigidity would be expected.

title: A presynaptic drug target
prompt: A researcher studies an antiseizure drug prescribed to a patient with focal epilepsy. The drug binds a protein involved in synaptic vesicle function rather than acting primarily through sodium-channel blockade. The prescribed drug is levetiracetam. Which target is implicated?
options: The benzodiazepine site on GABA-A receptors
explanation: Levetiracetam binds SV2A; its exact antiseizure mechanism is not fully established.

distractorExplanations.Synaptic vesicle protein SV2A: Levetiracetam binds SV2A; its exact antiseizure mechanism is not fully established.
distractorExplanations.Voltage-gated sodium channels: This is a major target of phenytoin, not the distinctive levetiracetam binding site.
distractorExplanations.Thalamic T-type calcium channels: This target is associated with ethosuximide.
distractorExplanations.The benzodiazepine site on GABA-A recept: Benzodiazepines act here; this is not SV2A.

title: Accumulation after renal decline
prompt: A 76-year-old man on stable levetiracetam therapy develops somnolence after dehydration-associated acute kidney injury. He has no focal neurologic deficit, hypoglycemia, or new sedative exposure. Which pharmacokinetic change most plausibly increases his exposure to the antiseizure medication?
options: Reduced renal elimination of unchanged drug
answer: Reduced renal elimination of unchanged drug

distractorExplanations.Reduced hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism: CYP3A4 is not its principal elimination pathway.
distractorExplanations.Increased renal clearance: This would lower, rather than increase, exposure.
distractorExplanations.Increased hepatic first-pass extraction: Greater first-pass removal would reduce oral systemic availability.
distractorExplanations.Increased elimination through bile: Greater elimination would not explain accumulation.

title: Behavioral change after seizure treatment
prompt: A 24-year-old man starts levetiracetam after recurrent focal seizures. At follow-up, his partner reports new irritability and aggressive outbursts beginning after treatment. He is alert, afebrile, and has no rigidity or autonomic instability. Which adverse effect should be considered first?
explanation: Irritability and aggression can emerge during levetiracetam treatment.

distractorExplanations.Levetiracetam-associated behavioral dist: Irritability and aggression can emerge during levetiracetam treatment.
distractorExplanations.Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: The exposure and characteristic rigidity and systemic illness are absent.
distractorExplanations.Serotonin syndrome: There is no serotonergic exposure, clonus, or hyperreflexia described.
distractorExplanations.Persistent postictal confusion: The sustained behavioral change does not follow a discrete recent seizure.
distractorExplanations.Antimuscarinic delirium: An alert patient without autonomic antimuscarinic findings is a poor fit.

title: Choosing a dose-adjustment variable
prompt: A 68-year-old woman with focal epilepsy is prescribed levetiracetam. She has chronic kidney disease and normal hepatic tests. The clinician reviews laboratory data before choosing her maintenance regimen. Which measurement is most directly relevant to the labeled renal dose adjustment?
explanation: Levetiracetam dosing in adults with renal impairment is adjusted using creatinine clearance.

distractorExplanations.Estimated creatinine clearance: Levetiracetam dosing in adults with renal impairment is adjusted using creatinine clearance.
distractorExplanations.Serum alanine aminotransferase: A hepatic injury marker does not quantify renal drug clearance.
distractorExplanations.International normalized ratio: This measures coagulation and is not the renal dosing variable.
distractorExplanations.Serum albumin alone: Albumin alone does not estimate renal filtration.
distractorExplanations.Serum alkaline phosphatase: This does not guide the labeled renal adjustment.

title: Stopping maintenance treatment
prompt: A 35-year-old woman has remained seizure-free on levetiracetam and asks about stopping therapy. After assessing her recurrence risk, her neurologist determines that withdrawal is appropriate. Which strategy best limits the medication-withdrawal risk in this nonemergency setting?
options: Abrupt discontinuation after the next dose
Alternating full-dose days with untreated days
Taking medication only when an aura occurs
Replacing each dose with an over-the-counter sleep aid
explanation: Gradual withdrawal helps limit increased seizure frequency and status epilepticus risk.

distractorExplanations.A supervised gradual taper: Gradual withdrawal helps limit increased seizure frequency and status epilepticus risk.
distractorExplanations.Abrupt discontinuation after the next do: Sudden withdrawal can increase seizure risk.
distractorExplanations.Alternating full-dose days with untreate: Irregular exposure is not a planned gradual taper.
distractorExplanations.Taking medication only when an aura occu: Maintenance therapy is not replaced by intermittent aura-triggered dosing.
distractorExplanations.Replacing each dose with an over-the-cou: A sleep aid does not provide equivalent antiseizure protection.
